````math
  §[3.3](#S3.SS3 "3.3 The two pitfalls and the conditioning invariant ‣ 3 Pitfalls: Two Default Ways to Train on an Edited Rollout ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")).
- •
  Naive-Compressed runs one forward on the compressed walk
  $`\mathbf{H}^{\mathrm{comp}}`$ and takes gradients at every response
  token. On $`\mathcal{T}`$ this collapses all branches into the final
  walk: the training forward sees $`\phi_{\mathrm{spine}}(v)`$, which at
  the $`D`$ diverging leaves is a *strict subset* of the live view
  $`\phi_{\mathrm{leg}}(v)`$ that generated the token — and, worse,
  contains summary content created after $`t`$. The loss on those leaves
  is therefore computed under conditioning the model never decoded from
  (Pitfall A,
  §[3.3](#S3.SS3 "3.3 The two pitfalls and the conditioning invariant ‣ 3 Pitfalls: Two Default Ways to Train on an Edited Rollout ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")).
- •
  LogitTree (ours, $`K`$-forward) runs one forward per branch layer, so
  $`K\!+\!1`$ forwards per rollout. Each forward covers a root-to-leaf
  path with $`\phi_{\mathrm{spine}}=\phi_{\mathrm{leg}}`$ along the
  entire branch (because the branch’s forward uses the *live view* as it
  existed during that layer). Gradients are placed on the leaves of that
  branch only, so the union of LogitTree’s gradient-carrying positions
  equals the leaf set of $`\mathcal{T}`$ without double-counting.
- •
  4D mask (ours, packed) realizes the same partition as LogitTree but in
  a *single* forward: one structured mask admits, in each query row,
  exactly the keys that were live when that token was decoded, so
  $`\phi_{\mathrm{spine}}=\phi_{\mathrm{leg}}`$ holds row by row and the
  branches share the tree trunk instead of being replayed. Gradient
  placement is identical to LogitTree’s; the difference is the pass
  count: one forward instead of $`K\!+\!1`$.
- •
  SDCC (ours) runs one student forward on $`\mathbf{H}^{\mathrm{comp}}`$
  (with gradient) plus one gradient-free teacher forward per branch
  layer that holds a diverging leaf — at most $`K`$, since the layer
  after $`J_{K}`$ re-converges. The policy-gradient loss remains on the
  student’s $`R`$-length response tokens. The consistency KL
  $`D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\pi_{\theta,\text{teach}}(\cdot\mid\mathbf{H}^{\prime}_{t})\,\|\,\pi_{\theta,\text{stud}}(\cdot\mid\mathbf{H}^{\mathrm{comp}}[:t]))`$
  is summed only over the $`D`$ diverging leaves, whose positions are
  given by the diverging-leaf mask constructed from the harness’s
  $`\{J_{k},E_{k}\}`$ records. On $`\mathcal{T}`$, SDCC pulls the
  student’s per-leaf distribution toward the teacher’s at exactly the
  diverging positions, without touching the trunk. This is where the
  $`O(\sqrt{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{KL}}})`$ bound of
  §[5.2](#S5.SS2 "5.2 What the residual KL guarantees ‣ 5 SDCC: Self-Distillation for Conditioning Consistency ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
  applies: as SDCC’s KL contracts, the student’s leaf distributions
  approach the teacher’s, and the diverging-leaf gap closes.

### B.3 Compute budget as tree traversal cost

Three lengths govern the budget: the union length
$`L=|\mathbf{H}_{T}|`$; the compressed walk
$`C=|\mathbf{H}^{\mathrm{comp}}|=L-|\bigcup_{k}E_{k}|`$, shorter than
$`L`$ by the token *mass* evicted and not by the eviction *count*; and
$`\ell_{i}`$, the live view in force during branch layer $`i`$.
Consecutive branches share the trunk, so $`C\leq\ell_{i}\leq L`$ — with
$`\ell_{K+1}=C`$, every eviction having fired by the last layer — and
$`\sum_{i=1}^{K+1}\ell_{i}\geq L`$ with equality only at $`K=0`$:
LogitTree re-reads the shared prefix once per layer rather than
splitting $`L`$ into $`K\!+\!1`$ disjoint pieces.
[Table 6](#A5.T6 "In Cost and applicability. ‣ E.2 Harnesses and methods ‣ Appendix E Implementation of the harnesses and the training methods ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
tabulates the resulting per-rollout pass and token budgets next to the
infrastructure each method demands.

Tokens are a proxy, not a cost: a forward over $`n`$ tokens costs
$`F(n)=\Theta(nd^{2}+n^{2}d)`$, and for Qwen3-4B the quadratic term
overtakes the linear one at $`n\approx 12`$k — inside the range of
contexts we observe
([Table 1](#S6.T1 "In Tree-consistent methods recover the drift floor; the two Naives inflate with eviction. ‣ 6.2 Grand result matrix (overview) ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")).
A dense kernel scores the packed sequence in full and discards the
masked entries, paying $`\Theta(L^{2}d)`$, while $`K\!+\!1`$ segmented
forwards pay $`\Theta(\sum_{i}\ell_{i}^{2}d)`$, so neither dominates —
it turns on the evicted mass. The 4D mask’s dependable advantage over
LogitTree is one backward instead of $`K\!+\!1`$ and one well-filled
kernel launch instead of $`K\!+\!1`$ short ones, not fewer FLOPs; a
genuine FLOP saving needs a block-sparse kernel. SDCC saves nothing on
the forward: because $`\ell_{K+1}=C`$, the student pass *is* the last
branch layer’s, and SDCC’s token budget $`C+\sum_{i=1}^{K}\ell_{i}`$
equals LogitTree’s $`\sum_{i=1}^{K+1}\ell_{i}`$ term for term. The
entire saving is the backward, $`1`$ instead of $`K{+}1`$; and unlike
either exact walk it gives up exactness, down to
$`\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{KL}}})`$.

### B.4 Per-leaf divergence and the two pitfalls

Recall that the editor fires repeatedly *inside* the rollout loop: at
step $`t`$ the policy sees the live view
$`\mathbf{H}^{\prime}_{t}=\textsc{View}_{t}(\mathbf{H}_{\leq t};\,\mathcal{E}_{\leq t})`$
of
equation [2](#S3.E2 "Equation 2 ‣ 3.2 Setup: the live view and the trajectory tree ‣ 3 Pitfalls: Two Default Ways to Train on an Edited Rollout ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
— the physical history with exactly the edits that have fired by step
$`t`$ applied, and no others — whereas the length-$`t`$ prefix
$`\mathbf{H}^{\mathrm{comp}}[:t]`$ of the final compressed walk
retroactively applies *future* edits $`\mathcal{E}_{>t}`$ to a token
generated before those edits existed.
[Table 4](#A2.T4 "In B.4 Per-leaf divergence and the two pitfalls ‣ Appendix B The trajectory tree: a unified structural analysis ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
instantiates the divergence for each leaf of the running example.

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
| Leaf $`y_{t}`$ | Live-view prefix $`\mathbf{p_{t}}(y_{t})`$ | Final-walk prefix $`\mathbf{p_{s}}(y_{t})`$ | Diverges by |
| $`y_{6}`$ | $`\{y_{1},y_{2},y_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}`$ | $`\{y_{1},y_{2},y_{3},y_{4}\}`$ | $`+\,y_{5}`$ |
| $`y_{7}`$ | $`\{y_{1},y_{2},y_{3},y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}`$ | $`\{y_{1},y_{2},y_{3},y_{4},y_{6}\}`$ | $`+\,y_{5}`$ |
| $`y_{9}`$ | $`\{y_{1},y_{2},y_{3},y_{4},y_{6},y_{7},y_{8}\}`$ | $`\{y_{1},y_{2},y_{3},y_{4},y_{6},y_{7}\}`$ | $`+\,y_{8}`$ |
| $`y_{10}`$ | $`\{y_{1},y_{2},y_{3},y_{4},y_{6},y_{7},y_{8},y_{9}\}`$ | $`\{y_{1},y_{2},y_{3},y_{4},y_{6},y_{7},y_{9}\}`$ | $`+\,y_{8}`$ |
| $`y_{12}`$ | $`\{y_{1},y_{2},y_{3},y_{4},y_{6},y_{7},y_{9},y_{10},y_{11}\}`$ | $`\{y_{1},y_{2},y_{3},y_{4},y_{6},y_{7},y_{9},y_{10}\}`$ | $`+\,y_{11}`$ |
| $`y_{\mathrm{ans}}`$ | $`\{y_{1},y_{2},y_{3},y_{4},y_{6},y_{7},y_{9},y_{10},y_{12}\}`$ | same | — |

Table 4: Per-leaf live-view prefix vs. final-walk prefix for the running
example ($`E_{1}=\{y_{5}\}`$ at $`J_{1}=7`$; $`E_{2}=\{y_{8}\}`$ at
$`J_{2}=10`$; $`E_{3}=\{y_{11}\}`$ at $`J_{3}=12`$). The leaf whose two
prefixes coincide ($`y_{\mathrm{ans}}`$) does not need any correction.
Evicting one token per junction keeps each row on a single line;
widening a span enlarges $`E_{k}`$ and each leaf’s eviction mass, but
changes neither which leaves diverge nor where the tree re-converges.

#### Pitfall A, SFT view (time-travel leakage).

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{SFT}}^{\mathrm{A}}\;=\;-\sum_{t}\log P_{\theta}(y_{t}\mid\mathbf{p_{s}}(y_{t}))\;\neq\;-\sum_{t}\log P_{\theta}(y_{t}\mid\mathbf{p_{t}}(y_{t}))\;=\;\mathcal{L}^{\star}_{\mathrm{SFT}}.
``` |  | (11) |

The model is fitted to a shorter-prefix distribution than the one that
generated the target token, while at inference the harness still
delivers the live view $`\mathbf{H}^{\prime}_{t}=\mathbf{p_{t}}(y_{t})`$
— a prefix the model was never trained to match.

#### Pitfall A, RL view (broken importance ratio).

The rollout policy sampled
$`a_{t}\sim\pi_{\theta_{\mathrm{old}}}(\cdot\mid\mathbf{p_{t}}(y_{t}))`$,
so the training ratio

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\rho_{t}^{\mathrm{A}}\;=\;\frac{\pi_{\theta}(a_{t}\mid\mathbf{p_{s}}(y_{t}))}{\pi_{\theta_{\mathrm{old}}}(a_{t}\mid\mathbf{p_{t}}(y_{t}))}\;\;\neq\;\;\frac{\pi_{\theta}(a_{t}\mid\mathbf{p_{t}}(y_{t}))}{\pi_{\theta_{\mathrm{old}}}(a_{t}\mid\mathbf{p_{t}}(y_{t}))}\;=\;\rho_{t}
``` |  | (12) |

invalidates PPO’s clip guarantee and mis-weights GRPO’s group-relative
advantage; empirically, the clip-rate map concentrates immediately after
each junction, precisely where the two prefixes diverge.

#### Pitfall B, SFT view (train–inference mismatch).

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{SFT}}^{\mathrm{B}}\;=\;-\sum_{t}\log P_{\theta}(y_{t}\mid\mathbf{H}_{<t}).
``` |  | (13) |

Cross-entropy is computed using a prefix that carries strictly more
information — including already-evicted content — than the deployed
model will ever see.

#### Pitfall B, RL view (advantage on the wrong observation).

Eventually-evicted tokens remain present during training, so they still
absorb a share of the outcome reward $`r_{\mathrm{out}}/T`$, and the
advantage baseline is fitted to $`V(\mathbf{H}_{<t})`$ instead of
$`V(\mathbf{H}^{\prime}_{t})`$; the step-level credit-assignment error
accumulates linearly in $`K`$ ([Jiang et al., 2025b](#bib.bib30)):

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\Exp\bigl[\|B_{e}^{(K)}\|_{2}\bigr]\simeq\varepsilon_{e}\cdot K\cdot\Exp\bigl[\|\nabla_{\theta}\log\pi_{\theta}(a_{e}\mid s_{e})\|_{2}\bigr],
``` |  | (14) |

where $`B_{e}^{(K)}`$ is the cumulative advantage-baseline bias at an
evicted-token position $`e`$ after $`K`$ eviction events occur along the
trajectory, and $`\varepsilon_{e}`$ is the per-event bias scale (the
misfit between $`V(\mathbf{H}_{t})`$ and $`V(\mathbf{H}^{\prime}_{t})`$
attributable to one evicted span).

[Table 5](#A2.T5 "In Pitfall B, RL view (advantage on the wrong observation). ‣ B.4 Per-leaf divergence and the two pitfalls ‣ Appendix B The trajectory tree: a unified structural analysis ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
summarizes the mirror symmetry of the two pitfalls; concrete per-leaf
examples (a $`\Delta_{\mathrm{comp}}=-22.8`$-nat leaf for Pitfall A and
a $`\Delta_{\mathrm{full}}=+18.5`$-nat leaf for Pitfall B, both on an
untrained Qwen3-4B) are provided in the main text
(§[3.3](#S3.SS3 "3.3 The two pitfalls and the conditioning invariant ‣ 3 Pitfalls: Two Default Ways to Train on an Edited Rollout ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")).

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  | Naive-Compressed (A) | Naive-Full (B) |
| Training input | $`\mathbf{H}^{\mathrm{comp}}`$ (rightmost path) | $`\mathbf{H}_{T}`$ (full DFS) |
| Prefix relation | $`c^{\mathrm{train}}\subsetneq c^{\mathrm{infer}}`$ | $`c^{\mathrm{train}}\supsetneq c^{\mathrm{infer}}`$ |
| Failure mode | time-travel leakage | train–inference mismatch |
| Directional signature | $`c`$ too short | $`c`$ too long |
| Intuition | “train saw less than infer” | “train saw future info” |
| Fixable by | any tree-consistent method | any tree-consistent method |

Table 5: Two symmetric failure modes of the same conditioning invariant.

For Qwen3-4B under live model-triggered compression
(§[6](#S6 "6 Experiments ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”"),
[Table 1](#S6.T1 "In Tree-consistent methods recover the drift floor; the two Naives inflate with eviction. ‣ 6.2 Grand result matrix (overview) ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")),
the mismatch is directly visible in the logdiff statistic: the
No-compression (Search-R1) control remains at $`0.014`$ (numerical noise
— with nothing compressed, the live view equals the physical history),
whereas Naive-Compressed rises to $`0.024`$–$`0.059`$ on average across
the three editors and peaks at $`0.23`$–$`0.29`$ on eviction-heavy
batches ($`{\sim}20\times`$ the baseline), scaling monotonically with
eviction density: the direct empirical signature of
$`c^{\mathrm{train}}\neq c^{\mathrm{infer}}`$, present from the very
first steps of training.

#### Correct gradients.

Under the invariant, both the supervised loss and the policy gradient
condition uniformly on $`\mathbf{H}^{\prime}_{t}`$ — the *observation*
of the editor-induced POMDP
(§[3.3](#S3.SS3 "3.3 The two pitfalls and the conditioning invariant ‣ 3 Pitfalls: Two Default Ways to Train on an Edited Rollout ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")):
the rollout and training policies in the importance ratio must share
this observation, and the advantage baseline must approximate
$`V(\mathbf{H}^{\prime}_{t})`$, not $`V(\mathbf{H}_{t})`$. A fix must
therefore restore
$`\nabla_{\theta}\widehat{\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{task}}}(\theta)=\nabla_{\theta}\mathcal{L}^{\star}_{\mathrm{task}}(\theta)`$
exactly
(§[2](#S4.F2 "Figure 2 ‣ 4 Exact Solutions: Two Ways to Walk the Context Tree ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”"))
or up to a quantifiable
$`\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{KL}}})`$ bias at the loss level
(§[5](#S5 "5 SDCC: Self-Distillation for Conditioning Consistency ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")).

## Appendix C Proofs

We proceed bottom-up: the per-branch tree decomposition
(§[C.1](#A3.SS1 "C.1 Per-branch equivalence on the tree ( and ) ‣ Appendix C Proofs ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”"))
is the primitive, the packed 4D construction
(§[C.2](#A3.SS2 "C.2 One packed forward reproduces the tree ( and ) ‣ Appendix C Proofs ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”"))
reproduces it in one masked forward, and their equivalence
(§[C.3](#A3.SS3 "C.3 Materialization equivalence () ‣ Appendix C Proofs ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”"))
follows. Every proof opens with a one-line sketch. Throughout,
$`\mathbf{p_{t}}(y_{t})=\mathbf{H}^{\prime}_{t}`$ is the live-view
root-to-leaf prefix of leaf $`y_{t}`$ in the conditioning tree
$`\mathcal{T}`$ of
[definition 2](#Thmdefinition2 "Definition 2 (Trajectory tree). ‣ B.1 Definition of the trajectory tree ‣ Appendix B The trajectory tree: a unified structural analysis ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”"),
and $`\mathbf{p_{s}}(y_{t})=\mathbf{H}^{\mathrm{comp}}[:t]`$ its prefix
on the final compressed walk.

### C.1 Per-branch equivalence on the tree ([propositions 3](#Thmproposition3 "Proposition 3 (SFT and RL equivalence on the tree). ‣ C.1 Per-branch equivalence on the tree ( and ) ‣ Appendix C Proofs ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”") and [3](#Thmproposition3 "Proposition 3 (SFT and RL equivalence on the tree). ‣ C.1 Per-branch equivalence on the tree ( and ) ‣ Appendix C Proofs ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”"))

###### Proposition 3 (SFT and RL equivalence on the tree).

Let $`\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{SFT}}^{\mathrm{tree}}`$ be the summed
cross-entropy over the $`K{+}1`$ per-branch forwards, each loss-masked
to its own branch. Then
$`\nabla_{\theta}\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{SFT}}^{\mathrm{tree}}=\sum_{\pi}\nabla_{\theta}\mathcal{L}^{\star}_{\mathrm{SFT}}(\mathbf{H}^{\prime\pi})`$.
For RL, the importance ratio, advantage baseline, and KL regularizer are
computed on the same $`\mathbf{H}^{\prime\pi}`$ during rollout and
update.

###### Proof.

*Sketch: the $`K{+}1`$ branches partition the loss-carrying leaves, so
regrouping the per-leaf loss by branch is an identity, not an
approximation.*

Each $`y_{t}`$ lies on exactly one branch $`\pi(y_{t})`$ — the one live
when it was produced — so
$`\mathbf{H}^{\prime\pi(y_{t})}[:t]=\mathbf{p_{t}}(y_{t})`$, and the
per-branch loss masks are disjoint and jointly exhaustive on the
response. Regrouping
$`\sum_{t}-\log P_{\theta}(y_{t}\mid\mathbf{p_{t}}(y_{t}))`$ by branch
returns $`\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{SFT}}^{\mathrm{tree}}`$ with no leaf
double-counted or missed, and the finite sum commutes with
$`\nabla_{\theta}`$. For
[Proposition 3](#Thmproposition3 "Proposition 3 (SFT and RL equivalence on the tree). ‣ C.1 Per-branch equivalence on the tree ( and ) ‣ Appendix C Proofs ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”"),
the importance ratio, advantage weight and KL regularizer at $`y_{t}`$
are all functions of $`P_{\theta}(\cdot\mid\mathbf{p_{t}}(y_{t}))`$,
which the branch-$`\pi`$ forward evaluates under exactly the
rollout-time conditioning. ∎

### C.2 One packed forward reproduces the tree ([propositions 4](#Thmproposition4 "Proposition 4 (SFT and RL equivalence for the 4D mask). ‣ C.2 One packed forward reproduces the tree ( and ) ‣ Appendix C Proofs ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”") and [4](#Thmproposition4 "Proposition 4 (SFT and RL equivalence for the 4D mask). ‣ C.2 One packed forward reproduces the tree ( and ) ‣ Appendix C Proofs ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”"))

###### Proposition 4 (SFT and RL equivalence for the 4D mask).

Suppose (i) $`M^{\mathrm{logical}}`$ exactly encodes logical visibility,
(ii) position ids are reassigned for each query row, (iii) loss and
attention masks are decoupled, (iv) no normalization crosses mask
boundaries, and (v) rollout and training share the same
$`M^{\mathrm{logical}}`$. Then, under dense softmax attention,
$`\nabla_{\theta}\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{SFT}}^{\mathrm{4D}}=\nabla_{\theta}\mathcal{L}^{\star}_{\mathrm{SFT}}`$,
and the importance ratio and KL regularizer are computed under identical
conditioning during rollout and update.

###### Proof.

*Sketch: a masked query row and its image in the compact sequence attend
to the same keys at the same relative offsets, hence produce the same
logits; induction over layers and the shared loss mask lift this to
gradient equality.*

Let $`\mathrm{Edit}`$ delete $`E_{t}\subset\mathbf{H}_{t}`$ and let
$`M`$ implement $`M^{\mathrm{logical}}`$ — the $`(T\times T)`$ mask of
§[4.2](#S4.SS2 "4.2 ❷The 4D attention mask packs all branches into one sequence ‣ 4 Exact Solutions: Two Ways to Walk the Context Tree ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
admitting key $`j`$ in row $`i`$ iff $`j`$ was live when $`y_{i}`$ was
decoded — so $`M_{ij}=-\infty`$ for $`j\in E_{t}`$, $`j<i`$, and causal
otherwise. By (iii) it suffices to prove
$`\mathbf{Logits}_{i}(\mathbf{H}_{t},M)=\mathbf{Logits}_{i}(\mathbf{H}^{\prime}_{t})`$
for $`i\notin E_{t}`$. Write $`i^{\prime},j^{\prime}`$ for the images of
$`i,j`$ under the deletion, so the visible set
$`V_{i}:=\{j<i:j\notin E_{t}\}`$ maps onto the prefix of the compact
sequence $`\mathbf{H}^{\prime}_{t}`$. Row $`i`$ mixes only over
$`V_{i}`$ by construction, and by (ii) the reassigned position ids give
$`(i,j)`$ the same relative offset as $`(i^{\prime},j^{\prime})`$; since
RoPE — or any relative-positional encoding — depends only on that
offset, $`q_{i}^{\top}k_{j}=q_{i^{\prime}}^{\top}k_{j^{\prime}}`$, so
softmax weights and mixed values agree. Condition (iv) closes the only
remaining channel of difference, per-token operations reading across
mask boundaries (a layer norm reduced over an unmasked axis, MoE routing
pooling evicted positions), so the residual stream at row $`i`$ equals
the compact-forward stream at $`i^{\prime}`$. Induction over layers
carries this to the unembedding, and the shared loss mask turns logit
equality into the gradient identity. ∎

### C.3 Materialization equivalence ([theorem 1](#Thmtheorem1 "Theorem 1 (Materialization equivalence). ‣ 4.3 ❸The centerpiece: 4D masks and LogitTree are the same walk ‣ 4 Exact Solutions: Two Ways to Walk the Context Tree ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”"))

*(Recalled.)* Under the assumptions of
[proposition 4](#Thmproposition4 "Proposition 4 (SFT and RL equivalence for the 4D mask). ‣ C.2 One packed forward reproduces the tree ( and ) ‣ Appendix C Proofs ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”"),
the 4D-masked single forward on the physical union $`\mathbf{H}_{T}`$
(§[4.2](#S4.SS2 "4.2 ❷The 4D attention mask packs all branches into one sequence ‣ 4 Exact Solutions: Two Ways to Walk the Context Tree ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”"))
and the $`K`$-segment logits-tree forward produce the same logits at
every non-evicted position.

###### Proof.

*Sketch: both materializations are the same scalar function of
$`\theta`$, and identical functions have identical gradients.*

By
[proposition 4](#Thmproposition4 "Proposition 4 (SFT and RL equivalence for the 4D mask). ‣ C.2 One packed forward reproduces the tree ( and ) ‣ Appendix C Proofs ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
each construction computes
$`\mathbf{Logits}_{i}(\mathbf{H}^{\prime}_{t})`$ at every loss-carrying
position under the identical loss mask; they differ only in cost (union
mask: one attention call with a $`(B,1,T,T)`$ structured mask; segmented
walk: $`K{+}1`$ separate forwards). Both losses are therefore the *same
scalar function of $`\theta`$* — the leaf sum
$`-\sum_{t}\log P_{\theta}(y_{t}\mid\mathbf{p_{t}}(y_{t}))`$ of
[proposition 3](#Thmproposition3 "Proposition 3 (SFT and RL equivalence on the tree). ‣ C.1 Per-branch equivalence on the tree ( and ) ‣ Appendix C Proofs ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
— so their gradients coincide up to floating-point association order. ∎

## Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss

This appendix derives the SDCC objective
(§[5](#S5 "5 SDCC: Self-Distillation for Conditioning Consistency ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”"),
Eq. equation [10](#S5.E10 "Equation 10 ‣ 5.1 Aligning the live and compressed trajectories ‣ 5 SDCC: Self-Distillation for Conditioning Consistency ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”"))
as a forward-KL conditioning-consistency (self-distillation)
regularizer, using amortized variational inference as a scaffold. The
correctness of SDCC does not rest on the ELBO being tight: it rests on
the zero set of the KL residual being exactly the conditioning invariant
(§[D.3](#A4.SS3 "D.3 Why the forward KL suffices ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")),
and on that residual controlling deployment behavior
(§[D.4](#A4.SS4 "D.4 How the KL residual controls deployment and gradient bias ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")).
§[5.1](#S5.SS1 "5.1 Aligning the live and compressed trajectories ‣ 5 SDCC: Self-Distillation for Conditioning Consistency ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
gives the main-text algorithmic view; here we state the assumptions and
give the proofs.

*Why the forward direction.* The slack in the ELBO is a *reverse* KL,
and descending it directly is the wake-phase update of amortized
inference ([Hinton et al., 1995](#bib.bib9); [Bornschein and Bengio,
2015](#bib.bib10)). At the sequence level that requires sampling whole
continuations from the *compressed* context: the resulting
score-function estimator is weighted by $`\log(q_{\theta}/p_{\theta})`$,
so its variance is unbounded on the surplus side, while the deficit side
— which is Pitfall A itself — is almost never drawn from the compressed
proposal and is therefore invisible to the update. SDCC instead descends
the forward-KL (sleep-phase) surrogate, which samples from the
well-behaved teacher side, has a plain bounded-variance cross-entropy
gradient, and, as
§[D.3](#A4.SS3 "D.3 Why the forward KL suffices ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
shows, has exactly the same zero set. The four subsections follow that
substitution:
§[D.1](#A4.SS1 "D.1 Probabilistic model and the conditioning invariant ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
fixes the probabilistic model,
§[D.2](#A4.SS2 "D.2 The ELBO and where the forward KL comes from ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
derives the bound the KL comes from,
§[D.3](#A4.SS3 "D.3 Why the forward KL suffices ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
shows the forward direction loses nothing, and
§[D.4](#A4.SS4 "D.4 How the KL residual controls deployment and gradient bias ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
bounds what a nonzero residual costs at deployment.

### D.1 Probabilistic model and the conditioning invariant

Fix a diverging leaf position $`p\in\mathcal{C}`$. All quantities below
are tied to this particular $`p`$; sums over $`\mathcal{C}`$ are taken
at the end. Write
$`\mathcal{A}(p)=\{k:\iota(E_{k})\leq p\leq e(E_{k})\}`$ for the
evictions active at $`p`$. The common case is $`|\mathcal{A}(p)|=1`$;
when several evictions are active the teacher context re-inserts every
span in $`\mathcal{A}(p)`$ and nothing below changes.

#### Random variables.

- •
  Clean context $`z_{p}:=\mathbf{p_{t}}(y_{p})`$: the pre-eviction
  prefix that was live at rollout time and that the harness will *again*
  deliver at deployment time. It is an *externally supplied*
  conditioning variable, never marginalized out: at inference the
  harness passes it directly to the policy.
- •
  Compressed context $`x_{p}:=\mathbf{p_{s}}(y_{p})\subsetneq z_{p}`$:
  the post-eviction prefix produced by the memory editor, which has
  removed every span in $`\mathcal{A}(p)`$.
- •
  Action $`y\in\mathcal{V}`$: the next generated token.
- •
  Outcome $`y^{\star}`$, with likelihood $`p(y^{\star}\mid y)`$: an
  oracle target for $`y`$. We take the RL reading as primary, in which
  $`\log p(y^{\star}\mid y)=r(y)/\tau`$ is the exponentiated-advantage
  log-likelihood of control-as-inference ([Levine, 2018](#bib.bib39));
  the SFT reading,
  $`\log p(y^{\star}\mid y)=\log\mathbf{1}[y=y^{\star}]`$, is its
  $`\tau\to 0`$ limit.¹¹ 1 The hard-indicator limit is degenerate as a
  variational target: whenever $`q_{\theta}`$ places mass off
  $`y^{\star}`$ the bound
  equation [18](#A4.E18 "Equation 18 ‣ Proposition 5 (Single-step ELBO for the amortized policy). ‣ D.2 The ELBO and where the forward KL comes from ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
  reads $`-\infty\geq-\infty`$ and is vacuously satisfied. Every
  statement below is made at finite $`\tau`$, where the expressions
  remain finite.

#### Distributions.

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle p_{\theta}(y\mid z_{p})`$ | $`\displaystyle:=P_{\theta}\bigl(\cdot\mid\mathbf{p_{t}}(y_{p})\bigr)`$ |  | deployed / target policy (teacher forward), |  | (15) |
|  | $`\displaystyle q_{\theta}(y\mid x_{p})`$ | $`\displaystyle:=P_{\theta}\bigl(\cdot\mid\mathbf{p_{s}}(y_{p})\bigr)_{p}`$ |  | amortized recognition policy (student forward), |  | (16) |
|  | $`\displaystyle p(y^{\star}\mid y)`$ |  |  | outcome likelihood given action. |  | (17) |

The two policies share parameters $`\theta`$; the amortization is
*parametric*, not architectural. The conditioning invariant of
§[3.3](#S3.SS3 "3.3 The two pitfalls and the conditioning invariant ‣ 3 Pitfalls: Two Default Ways to Train on an Edited Rollout ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
is the statement that this amortization is exact,

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
q_{\theta}(\cdot\mid x_{p})\;=\;p_{\theta}(\cdot\mid z_{p})\qquad\forall\,p\in\mathcal{C}.
``` |  | (CI) |

equation [CI](#A4.Ex4 "Equation CI ‣ Distributions. ‣ D.1 Probabilistic model and the conditioning invariant ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
is not a modeling assumption — it is the condition we want to *achieve*
through training, and everything that follows is an argument that the
SDCC penalty achieves it.

### D.2 The ELBO and where the forward KL comes from

This subsection does three things. It derives the variational bound
whose slack is the conditioning gap and shows that slack to be an exact
KL divergence; it identifies the multiplier $`\lambda`$ of
equation [10](#S5.E10 "Equation 10 ‣ 5.1 Aligning the live and compressed trajectories ‣ 5 SDCC: Self-Distillation for Conditioning Consistency ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
as the $`\beta`$ of a $`\beta`$-VAE free energy, which fixes both its
interpretation and its failure mode at large values; and it shows why
that slack cannot be descended in the direction the bound presents it in
— the fact that forces the forward-KL substitution justified in
§[D.3](#A4.SS3 "D.3 Why the forward KL suffices ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”").

###### Proposition 5 (Single-step ELBO for the amortized policy).

For every $`\theta`$ and every diverging leaf $`p\in\mathcal{C}`$,

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\log p_{\theta}(y^{\star}\mid z_{p})\;\geq\;\Exp_{y\sim q_{\theta}(\cdot\mid x_{p})}\!\bigl[\log p(y^{\star}\mid y)\bigr]\;-\;D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\Bigl(q_{\theta}(\cdot\mid x_{p})\,\big\|\,p_{\theta}(\cdot\mid z_{p})\Bigr),
``` |  | (18) |

with equality iff
$`q_{\theta}(\cdot\mid x_{p})=p_{\theta}(\cdot\mid y^{\star},z_{p})`$
almost everywhere.

###### Proof.

Marginalizing the action gives the evidence
$`p_{\theta}(y^{\star}\mid z_{p})=\sum_{y}p(y^{\star}\mid y)\,p_{\theta}(y\mid z_{p})`$.
Multiplying and dividing by $`q_{\theta}(y\mid x_{p})`$, rewriting the
sum as a $`q_{\theta}`$-expectation and applying Jensen to the concave
logarithm,

|  |  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle\log p_{\theta}(y^{\star}\mid z_{p})`$ | $`\displaystyle\;=\;\log\Exp_{y\sim q_{\theta}}\!\left[\frac{p(y^{\star}\mid y)\,p_{\theta}(y\mid z_{p})}{q_{\theta}(y\mid x_{p})}\right]\;\geq\;\Exp_{y\sim q_{\theta}}\!\left[\log\frac{p(y^{\star}\mid y)\,p_{\theta}(y\mid z_{p})}{q_{\theta}(y\mid x_{p})}\right]`$ |  | (19) |
|  |  | $`\displaystyle\;=\;\Exp_{y\sim q_{\theta}}\!\bigl[\log p(y^{\star}\mid y)\bigr]\;-\;D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\bigl(q_{\theta}(\cdot\mid x_{p})\,\big\|\,p_{\theta}(\cdot\mid z_{p})\bigr),`$ |  |  |

which is
equation [18](#A4.E18 "Equation 18 ‣ Proposition 5 (Single-step ELBO for the amortized policy). ‣ D.2 The ELBO and where the forward KL comes from ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”").
The importance-weighting step needs the proposal
$`q_{\theta}(\cdot\mid x_{p})`$ to dominate the integrand; this is
automatic here, since both distributions are softmax outputs of the same
network and so have full support on $`\mathcal{V}`$ (up to numerical
underflow). The reverse domination — $`p_{\theta}(\cdot\mid z_{p})`$
dominating $`q_{\theta}(\cdot\mid x_{p})`$ — is *not* needed for the
bound, and is precisely what fails for the reverse-KL estimator below.

For the equality condition, observe that the Jensen gap is itself a KL
divergence. Bayes’ rule at fixed $`z_{p}`$ reads
$`p_{\theta}(y\mid y^{\star},z_{p})=p(y^{\star}\mid y)\,p_{\theta}(y\mid z_{p})/p_{\theta}(y^{\star}\mid z_{p})`$,
so
$`\log p_{\theta}(y^{\star}\mid z_{p})=\log p(y^{\star}\mid y)+\log p_{\theta}(y\mid z_{p})-\log p_{\theta}(y\mid y^{\star},z_{p})`$
for every $`y`$ in the support. The left-hand side does not depend on
$`y`$, so it is unchanged by taking the $`q_{\theta}`$-expectation of
the right-hand side; adding and subtracting
$`\Exp_{q_{\theta}}[\log q_{\theta}(y\mid x_{p})]`$ and regrouping the
three resulting expectations gives the *exact* decomposition

|  |  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle\log p_{\theta}(y^{\star}\mid z_{p})\;=`$ | $`\displaystyle\underbrace{\Exp_{q_{\theta}}\bigl[\log p(y^{\star}\mid y)\bigr]-D_{\mathrm{KL}}\bigl(q_{\theta}(\cdot\mid x_{p})\,\|\,p_{\theta}(\cdot\mid z_{p})\bigr)}_{\text{the bound }equation~\ref{eq:app:elbo}}`$ |  | (20) |
|  |  | $`\displaystyle+\;\underbrace{D_{\mathrm{KL}}\bigl(q_{\theta}(\cdot\mid x_{p})\,\|\,p_{\theta}(\cdot\mid y^{\star},z_{p})\bigr)}_{\text{tightness gap, against the outcome-conditioned posterior}}.`$ |  |  |

The residual term is non-negative by Gibbs’ inequality — which
re-derives
equation [18](#A4.E18 "Equation 18 ‣ Proposition 5 (Single-step ELBO for the amortized policy). ‣ D.2 The ELBO and where the forward KL comes from ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
without invoking Jensen — and vanishes iff
$`q_{\theta}(\cdot\mid x_{p})=p_{\theta}(\cdot\mid y^{\star},z_{p})`$
a.e. ∎

#### Reading the bound.

The first term of
equation [18](#A4.E18 "Equation 18 ‣ Proposition 5 (Single-step ELBO for the amortized policy). ‣ D.2 The ELBO and where the forward KL comes from ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
is the (negated) task loss evaluated under the compressed conditioning
that training actually sees; the second is the *conditioning gap*
between the compressed and pre-eviction views, and it is the only term
that references $`z_{p}`$. Decomposition
equation [20](#A4.E20 "Equation 20 ‣ Proof. ‣ D.2 The ELBO and where the forward KL comes from ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
is worth isolating because it separates two quantities that are easy to
conflate in the main text: the conditioning gap, which SDCC exists to
close, and the tightness gap
$`D_{\mathrm{KL}}(q_{\theta}(\cdot\mid x_{p})\|p_{\theta}(\cdot\mid y^{\star},z_{p}))`$
against the *outcome-conditioned* posterior, which SDCC never touches
and does not need to.
§[D.3](#A4.SS3 "D.3 Why the forward KL suffices ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
makes that separation precise.

#### The multiplier $`\lambda`$ is the $`\beta`$ of a $`\beta`$-VAE.

Nothing in
equation [18](#A4.E18 "Equation 18 ‣ Proposition 5 (Single-step ELBO for the amortized policy). ‣ D.2 The ELBO and where the forward KL comes from ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
fixes the relative weight of its two terms. Treating the conditioning
gap as a *constraint* rather than a fixed-weight penalty — maximize the
task evidence subject to
$`\sum_{p\in\mathcal{C}}D_{\mathrm{KL}}\leq\delta`$ — and forming the
Lagrangian returns
equation [10](#S5.E10 "Equation 10 ‣ 5.1 Aligning the live and compressed trajectories ‣ 5 SDCC: Self-Distillation for Conditioning Consistency ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
exactly, with $`\lambda`$ the multiplier and the constant
$`\lambda\delta`$ discarded. In $`\beta`$-VAE terms ([Higgins et al.,
2017](#bib.bib37)), writing $`\beta:=\lambda`$ and using the task loss
as the distortion,

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathcal{F}_{\beta}(\theta)\;=\;\underbrace{\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{task}}(\theta;\mathbf{H}^{\mathrm{comp}})}_{\text{distortion}}\;+\;\beta\sum_{p\in\mathcal{C}}\underbrace{D_{\mathrm{KL}}\bigl(p_{\mathrm{sg}(\theta)}(\cdot\mid z_{p})\,\big\|\,q_{\theta}(\cdot\mid x_{p})\bigr)}_{\text{rate}},
``` |  | (21) |

with $`\beta=1`$ the plain evidence bound and $`\beta=0`$
Naive-Compressed. The distortion–rate tension is genuine here precisely
because $`x_{p}\subsetneq z_{p}`$: distortion is minimized by exploiting
the compressed tokens, rate by making the student’s output independent
of them, and any task-relevant content of $`z_{p}\setminus x_{p}`$ must
be recovered through the parameters rather than read off the input.
Pushing $`\beta`$ too far therefore reproduces the classical failure
mode.

###### Proposition 6 (Collapse regime at large $`\beta`$).

Let $`\theta^{\mathrm{coll}}`$ be a parameter at which the student
output is functionally independent of $`x_{p}`$ and equals the teacher,
$`q_{\theta^{\mathrm{coll}}}(\cdot\mid x_{p})=p_{\mathrm{sg}(\theta^{\mathrm{coll}})}(\cdot\mid z_{p})`$
for all $`p\in\mathcal{C}`$. Then the rate term of
equation [21](#A4.E21 "Equation 21 ‣ The multiplier 𝜆 is the 𝛽 of a 𝛽-VAE. ‣ D.2 The ELBO and where the forward KL comes from ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
vanishes at $`\theta^{\mathrm{coll}}`$ while its distortion term is
generically positive, and for every
$`\beta>\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{task}}(\theta^{\mathrm{coll}};\mathbf{H}^{\mathrm{comp}})/\varepsilon^{\star}`$
— where $`\varepsilon^{\star}>0`$ lower-bounds the rate at a
task-optimal $`\theta^{\star}`$ — one has
$`\mathcal{F}_{\beta}(\theta^{\mathrm{coll}})<\mathcal{F}_{\beta}(\theta^{\star})`$,
so descent on $`\mathcal{F}_{\beta}`$ from an uninformed initialization
is attracted to the collapsed solution.

###### Proof.

The rate vanishes at $`\theta^{\mathrm{coll}}`$ by construction. The
distortion is positive because a student that ignores $`x_{p}`$ cannot
fit a task loss evaluated on $`\mathbf{H}^{\mathrm{comp}}`$.
Substituting both into
equation [21](#A4.E21 "Equation 21 ‣ The multiplier 𝜆 is the 𝛽 of a 𝛽-VAE. ‣ D.2 The ELBO and where the forward KL comes from ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
gives
$`\mathcal{F}_{\beta}(\theta^{\mathrm{coll}})=\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{task}}(\theta^{\mathrm{coll}};\mathbf{H}^{\mathrm{comp}})`$,
while
$`\mathcal{F}_{\beta}(\theta^{\star})\geq\beta\varepsilon^{\star}`$; the
stated threshold on $`\beta`$ is exactly the crossing point. This is
$`\beta`$-VAE posterior collapse ([Alemi et al., 2018](#bib.bib38);
[Razavi et al., 2019](#bib.bib41)). ∎

Prop. [6](#Thmproposition6 "Proposition 6 (Collapse regime at large 𝛽). ‣ The multiplier 𝜆 is the 𝛽 of a 𝛽-VAE. ‣ D.2 The ELBO and where the forward KL comes from ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
is why $`\lambda`$ carries a warm-up schedule and the target a
stop-gradient rather than being a free hyperparameter: KL annealing
holds $`\beta=0`$ until task-loss SGD has moved off
$`\theta^{\mathrm{coll}}`$, and a frozen (or EMA) target keeps it from
tracking the student into collapse. Both are the standard $`\beta`$-VAE
remedies, and both are analyzed in
§[D.6](#A4.SS6 "D.6 Convergence: contraction toward the zero-KL set ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”").

#### Why the slack cannot be descended in the direction it appears.

The remaining step is the direction of the KL. The obvious move is to
descend the term of
equation [18](#A4.E18 "Equation 18 ‣ Proposition 5 (Single-step ELBO for the amortized policy). ‣ D.2 The ELBO and where the forward KL comes from ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
as written — the *wake-phase* update of amortized inference ([Hinton et
al., 1995](#bib.bib9); [Bornschein and Bengio, 2015](#bib.bib10)).
Because the gradient must then pass through the sampling distribution,
its estimator is a score function reweighted by a log-ratio.

###### Lemma 1 (Wake-phase gradient, and the variance of its estimator).

Let
$`L^{\mathrm{wake}}(\theta):=D_{\mathrm{KL}}\bigl(q_{\theta}(\cdot\mid x_{p})\,\|\,p_{\mathrm{sg}(\theta)}(\cdot\mid z_{p})\bigr)`$
with the target branch frozen, and write
$`g_{\theta}(y):=\nabla_{\theta}\log q_{\theta}(y\mid x_{p})`$ and
$`\rho_{\theta}(y):=q_{\theta}(y\mid x_{p})/p_{\mathrm{sg}(\theta)}(y\mid z_{p})`$.
Then

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\nabla_{\theta}L^{\mathrm{wake}}(\theta)\;=\;\Exp_{y\sim q_{\theta}}\bigl[\log\rho_{\theta}(y)\,g_{\theta}(y)\bigr],
``` |  | (22) |

and its $`N`$-sample Monte-Carlo estimator has variance

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\Var\bigl[\widehat{\nabla_{\theta}L^{\mathrm{wake}}}\bigr]\;=\;\frac{1}{N}\Bigl(\Exp_{q_{\theta}}\bigl[(\log\rho_{\theta})^{2}\,\|g_{\theta}\|^{2}\bigr]-\bigl\|\Exp_{q_{\theta}}\bigl[\log\rho_{\theta}\,g_{\theta}\bigr]\bigr\|^{2}\Bigr).
``` |  | (23) |

###### Proof.

$`L^{\mathrm{wake}}(\theta)=\sum_{y}q_{\theta}(y\mid x_{p})\log\rho_{\theta}(y)`$,
and only $`q_{\theta}`$ carries a gradient, so
$`\nabla_{\theta}L^{\mathrm{wake}}=\sum_{y}\nabla_{\theta}q_{\theta}(y)\log\rho_{\theta}(y)+\sum_{y}\nabla_{\theta}q_{\theta}(y)`$.
The log-derivative identity
$`\nabla_{\theta}q_{\theta}=q_{\theta}\,g_{\theta}`$ turns the first sum
into
equation [22](#A4.E22 "Equation 22 ‣ Lemma 1 (Wake-phase gradient, and the variance of its estimator). ‣ Why the slack cannot be descended in the direction it appears. ‣ D.2 The ELBO and where the forward KL comes from ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”"),
and the second is
$`\nabla_{\theta}\sum_{y}q_{\theta}(y)=\nabla_{\theta}1=0`$. Equation
equation [23](#A4.E23 "Equation 23 ‣ Lemma 1 (Wake-phase gradient, and the variance of its estimator). ‣ Why the slack cannot be descended in the direction it appears. ‣ D.2 The ELBO and where the forward KL comes from ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
is then the variance of a mean of $`N`$ i.i.d. copies of
$`X:=\log\rho_{\theta}(y)\,g_{\theta}(y)`$, namely
$`(\Exp\|X\|^{2}-\|\Exp X\|^{2})/N`$. ∎

Identity
equation [23](#A4.E23 "Equation 23 ‣ Lemma 1 (Wake-phase gradient, and the variance of its estimator). ‣ Why the slack cannot be descended in the direction it appears. ‣ D.2 The ELBO and where the forward KL comes from ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
is exact — it uses no $`\log\rho\approx\rho-1`$ small-ratio expansion —
and it exposes two failure modes, one on each side of the eviction:

- •
  Surplus side: unbounded variance. A token $`y^{\dagger}`$ the
  compressed context finds plausible
  ($`q_{\theta}(y^{\dagger}\mid x_{p})\geq q_{0}>0`$) but the
  pre-eviction context does not
  ($`p_{\mathrm{sg}(\theta)}(y^{\dagger}\mid z_{p})\to 0`$) — a
  redundant re-query that looks reasonable only once the retrieved span
  is gone — sends $`\log\rho_{\theta}(y^{\dagger})\to+\infty`$, and the
  second moment in
  equation [23](#A4.E23 "Equation 23 ‣ Lemma 1 (Wake-phase gradient, and the variance of its estimator). ‣ Why the slack cannot be descended in the direction it appears. ‣ D.2 The ELBO and where the forward KL comes from ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
  grows like $`(\log\rho_{\theta}(y^{\dagger}))^{2}`$. No variance bound
  holds uniformly over $`\Theta`$.
- •
  Deficit side: sampling blindness. A token the pre-eviction context
  supports
  ($`p_{\mathrm{sg}(\theta)}(y^{\dagger}\mid z_{p})\geq p_{0}>0`$) but
  the compressed one has lost
  ($`q_{\theta}(y^{\dagger}\mid x_{p})\to 0`$) is Pitfall A itself. Here
  the variance does *not* blow up, since $`q\log^{2}q\to 0`$, and that
  is exactly the problem: the summand
  $`q_{\theta}(y^{\dagger})\log\rho_{\theta}(y^{\dagger})g_{\theta}(y^{\dagger})\to 0`$,
  so the update draws no signal from the one token whose conditioning it
  is meant to repair, and an $`N`$-sample estimator needs
  $`N=\Omega\bigl(1/q_{\theta}(y^{\dagger})\bigr)`$ draws to observe it
  even once.

Both are properties of the sequence-level Monte-Carlo estimator rather
than of the reverse KL as a function: a per-token vocabulary sum
evaluates $`L^{\mathrm{wake}}`$ exactly and has neither pathology. What
survives even in that exact form is the reverse direction’s zero-forcing
bias, which under-covers precisely the modes an eviction removes. Two
substitutions therefore separate
equation [18](#A4.E18 "Equation 18 ‣ Proposition 5 (Single-step ELBO for the amortized policy). ‣ D.2 The ELBO and where the forward KL comes from ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
from
equation [10](#S5.E10 "Equation 10 ‣ 5.1 Aligning the live and compressed trajectories ‣ 5 SDCC: Self-Distillation for Conditioning Consistency ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
— the KL is taken forward rather than reverse, and its right argument is
frozen by a stop-gradient — and
§[D.3](#A4.SS3 "D.3 Why the forward KL suffices ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
justifies both, showing that the forward direction samples from the
well-behaved side, has a bounded-variance gradient, and retains the same
zero set.

### D.3 Why the forward KL suffices

Two things must hold before the ELBO’s reverse KL may be replaced by the
forward KL that SDCC minimizes: the reverse-KL slack must vanish exactly
at the conditioning invariant, so that the ELBO points at the right
target; and the forward KL must have the same zero set, so that the
substitution loses nothing.

#### The slack is the conditioning gap, and is weaker than tightness.

###### Proposition 7 (Slack-zero implication).

$`D_{\mathrm{KL}}\bigl(q_{\theta}(\cdot\mid x_{p})\,\|\,p_{\theta}(\cdot\mid z_{p})\bigr)=0`$
if and only if
$`q_{\theta}(\cdot\mid x_{p})=p_{\theta}(\cdot\mid z_{p})`$ a.e., i.e.
if and only if the per-leaf conditioning
invariant equation [CI](#A4.Ex4 "Equation CI ‣ Distributions. ‣ D.1 Probabilistic model and the conditioning invariant ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
holds. This is *strictly weaker* than tightness of
equation [18](#A4.E18 "Equation 18 ‣ Proposition 5 (Single-step ELBO for the amortized policy). ‣ D.2 The ELBO and where the forward KL comes from ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”"),
which by
Prop. [5](#Thmproposition5 "Proposition 5 (Single-step ELBO for the amortized policy). ‣ D.2 The ELBO and where the forward KL comes from ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
additionally requires the recognition policy to equal the
*outcome-conditioned* posterior
$`p_{\theta}(\cdot\mid y^{\star},z_{p})`$ rather than the
outcome-marginal $`p_{\theta}(\cdot\mid z_{p})`$.²² 2 The two targets
coincide only when $`p(y^{\star}\mid y)`$ is $`y`$-independent on the
support of $`p_{\theta}(\cdot\mid z_{p})`$, i.e. when the outcome
carries no discriminative signal — a degenerate configuration, and not
the regime of interest here.

###### Proof.

Gibbs’ inequality gives the first equivalence: a KL divergence is zero
iff its two arguments coincide almost everywhere. The second claim is
the equality condition of
Prop. [5](#Thmproposition5 "Proposition 5 (Single-step ELBO for the amortized policy). ‣ D.2 The ELBO and where the forward KL comes from ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”").
∎

The ELBO is therefore scaffolding rather than the object of interest:
driving its slack to zero closes the amortization gap between the two
conditioning distributions *without* tightening the bound, and SDCC’s
justification needs only the former.

#### The sleep-phase surrogate.

Wake–sleep ([Hinton et al., 1995](#bib.bib9)) flips the sampling
direction: instead of sampling from $`q_{\theta}`$ and fitting it to
$`p_{\theta}`$, it samples from the frozen $`p_{\mathrm{sg}(\theta)}`$
and fits $`q_{\theta}`$ by maximum likelihood on those samples.

###### Proposition 8 (The sleep-phase update is a forward KL and recovers equation [10](#S5.E10 "Equation 10 ‣ 5.1 Aligning the live and compressed trajectories ‣ 5 SDCC: Self-Distillation for Conditioning Consistency ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")).

Let
$`L^{\mathrm{sleep}}(\theta):=\Exp_{y\sim p_{\mathrm{sg}(\theta)}(\cdot\mid z_{p})}\bigl[-\log q_{\theta}(y\mid x_{p})\bigr]`$.
Then

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
L^{\mathrm{sleep}}(\theta)\;=\;D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\Bigl(p_{\mathrm{sg}(\theta)}(\cdot\mid z_{p})\,\big\|\,q_{\theta}(\cdot\mid x_{p})\Bigr)\;+\;H\!\bigl(p_{\mathrm{sg}(\theta)}(\cdot\mid z_{p})\bigr),
``` |  | (24) |

with $`H(\cdot)`$ the Shannon entropy. Since the stop-gradient makes the
entropy $`\theta`$-independent,
$`\nabla_{\theta}L^{\mathrm{sleep}}=\nabla_{\theta}D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p_{\mathrm{sg}(\theta)}\,\|\,q_{\theta})=-\Exp_{y\sim p_{\mathrm{sg}(\theta)}}[\nabla_{\theta}\log q_{\theta}(y\mid x_{p})]`$,
a plain cross-entropy score whose $`N`$-sample Monte-Carlo estimator has
variance at most
$`\Exp_{y\sim p_{\mathrm{sg}(\theta)}}\|\nabla_{\theta}\log q_{\theta}(y\mid x_{p})\|^{2}/N`$
— no $`q/p`$ re-weighting appears. Summing over $`p\in\mathcal{C}`$ and
adding the task loss recovers the boxed SDCC objective
equation [10](#S5.E10 "Equation 10 ‣ 5.1 Aligning the live and compressed trajectories ‣ 5 SDCC: Self-Distillation for Conditioning Consistency ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
verbatim:

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{SDCC{}}}(\theta)\;=\;\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{task}}(\theta;\mathbf{H}^{\mathrm{comp}})\;+\;\lambda\sum_{p\in\mathcal{C}}D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\Bigl(\underbrace{p_{\mathrm{sg}(\theta)}(\cdot\mid z_{p})}_{\text{teacher, stop-grad}}\,\Big\|\,\underbrace{q_{\theta}(\cdot\mid x_{p})}_{\text{student, with-grad}}\Bigr).
``` |  | (25) |

###### Proof sketch.

Add and subtract $`\log p_{\mathrm{sg}(\theta)}(y\mid z_{p})`$ inside
the expectation defining $`L^{\mathrm{sleep}}`$ and identify the two
resulting expectations as a KL divergence and an entropy; that is
equation [24](#A4.E24 "Equation 24 ‣ Proposition 8 (The sleep-phase update is a forward KL and recovers equation ). ‣ The sleep-phase surrogate. ‣ D.3 Why the forward KL suffices ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”").
Differentiating with the target held fixed leaves the score expectation
stated, whose estimator variance is its second moment; the bound is
finite because $`q_{\theta}`$ has full support (softmax) and no
ratio-based re-weighting inflates the summand. For the last claim, sum
equation [24](#A4.E24 "Equation 24 ‣ Proposition 8 (The sleep-phase update is a forward KL and recovers equation ). ‣ The sleep-phase surrogate. ‣ D.3 Why the forward KL suffices ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
over $`p\in\mathcal{C}`$, discard the $`\theta`$-independent entropy
sum, weight the KL sum by $`\lambda`$, add the task loss, and substitute
$`q_{\theta}(\cdot\mid x_{p})=P_{\theta}(\cdot\mid\mathbf{p_{s}}(y_{p}))_{p}`$
and
$`p_{\mathrm{sg}(\theta)}(\cdot\mid z_{p})=P^{\mathrm{target}}(\cdot\mid\mathbf{p_{t}}(y_{p}))`$
with the notation of
§[5.1](#S5.SS1 "5.1 Aligning the live and compressed trajectories ‣ 5 SDCC: Self-Distillation for Conditioning Consistency ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”").
∎

#### The two directions have the same zero set.

###### Theorem 2 (Zero SDCC residual $`\Leftrightarrow`$ conditioning invariant).

Let
$`\varepsilon_{p}(\theta):=D_{\mathrm{KL}}\bigl(p_{\mathrm{sg}(\theta)}(\cdot\mid z_{p})\,\|\,q_{\theta}(\cdot\mid x_{p})\bigr)`$
be the per-leaf forward-KL residual that SDCC minimizes. Then

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\bigl(p_{\mathrm{sg}(\theta)}\,\big\|\,q_{\theta}\bigr)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad p_{\mathrm{sg}(\theta)}=q_{\theta}\;\text{ a.e.}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad D_{\mathrm{KL}}\bigl(q_{\theta}\,\big\|\,p_{\mathrm{sg}(\theta)}\bigr)=0,
``` |  | (26) |

and consequently $`\sum_{p\in\mathcal{C}}\varepsilon_{p}(\theta)=0`$ if
and only if the conditioning
invariant equation [CI](#A4.Ex4 "Equation CI ‣ Distributions. ‣ D.1 Probabilistic model and the conditioning invariant ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
holds at every diverging leaf — in which case the ELBO’s reverse-KL
slack of
Prop. [7](#Thmproposition7 "Proposition 7 (Slack-zero implication). ‣ The slack is the conditioning gap, and is weaker than tightness. ‣ D.3 Why the forward KL suffices ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
is zero as well.

###### Proof.

Both equivalences in
equation [26](#A4.E26 "Equation 26 ‣ Theorem 2 (Zero SDCC residual ⇔ conditioning invariant). ‣ The two directions have the same zero set. ‣ D.3 Why the forward KL suffices ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
are Gibbs’ inequality: a KL divergence vanishes iff its two arguments
agree almost everywhere, and that condition is symmetric in the two
arguments even though the two divergences are not. A sum of non-negative
terms is zero iff every term is, which lifts the per-leaf statement to
$`\mathcal{C}`$. ∎

Away from the zero set the two divergences are different functions of
$`\theta`$, and the forward direction is the one that can actually be
descended in a single-backward training loop: the frozen teacher
supplies the target distribution, the gradient flows only through the
student, and the update is an ordinary cross-entropy rather than a
$`\log(q_{\theta}/p_{\theta})`$-weighted score-function estimator whose
variance diverges exactly on the tokens the eviction damaged. Full ELBO
tightness
(Prop. [5](#Thmproposition5 "Proposition 5 (Single-step ELBO for the amortized policy). ‣ D.2 The ELBO and where the forward KL comes from ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”"))
is strictly stronger than
equation [26](#A4.E26 "Equation 26 ‣ Theorem 2 (Zero SDCC residual ⇔ conditioning invariant). ‣ The two directions have the same zero set. ‣ D.3 Why the forward KL suffices ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
and is neither targeted nor required.

#### Existence of a zero-KL solution.

The residual can be driven to zero at all only if the model can
reproduce its pre-eviction conditional from the compressed prefix alone.

###### Proposition 9 (Existence of a zero-KL solution).

If model capacity admits $`\theta^{\star}`$ with
$`P_{\theta^{\star}}(\cdot\mid\mathbf{p_{s}}(y_{p}))_{p}=P_{\theta^{\star}}(\cdot\mid\mathbf{p_{t}}(y_{p}))`$
for all $`p\in\mathcal{C}`$, then the SDCC KL loss attains $`0`$. This
holds when the evicted span is redundant with the surviving trunk, and
fails when the span carries a strictly necessary bit absent from
$`\mathbf{H}^{\mathrm{comp}}`$, in which case $`\varepsilon_{p}`$ stays
positive and SDCC is bias-dominated relative to the exact methods.

###### Proof.

Each per-leaf term $`\varepsilon_{p}(\theta)`$ is non-negative, so
$`K(\theta)=\sum_{p\in\mathcal{C}}\varepsilon_{p}(\theta)\geq 0`$ with
equality iff student and teacher coincide on every diverging leaf
([theorem 2](#Thmtheorem2 "Theorem 2 (Zero SDCC residual ⇔ conditioning invariant). ‣ The two directions have the same zero set. ‣ D.3 Why the forward KL suffices ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”"));
whenever capacity admits such a $`\theta^{\star}`$ the zero set
$`\Theta_{K}`$ is non-empty and the loss attains $`0`$. This is
existence only — that SGD reaches it is
[theorem 4](#Thmtheorem4 "Theorem 4 (Steady-state contraction toward zero-KL set). ‣ Steady-state contraction. ‣ D.6 Convergence: contraction toward the zero-KL set ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
in
[section D.6](#A4.SS6 "D.6 Convergence: contraction toward the zero-KL set ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”"),
at rate $`\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{T})`$ to the noise floor and exactly $`0`$
under the decaying-step-size schedule of
[corollary 3](#Thmcorollary3 "Corollary 3 (Conditioning bias rate). ‣ EMA targets. ‣ D.6 Convergence: contraction toward the zero-KL set ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”").
∎

### D.4 How the KL residual controls deployment and gradient bias

In finite training the residual $`\varepsilon_{p}(\theta)`$ is small but
nonzero, so what matters is not the zero set of
[theorem 2](#Thmtheorem2 "Theorem 2 (Zero SDCC residual ⇔ conditioning invariant). ‣ The two directions have the same zero set. ‣ D.3 Why the forward KL suffices ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
but the chain *small KL $`\Rightarrow`$ small total variation
$`\Rightarrow`$ small deployment deviation $`\Rightarrow`$ small
policy-gradient bias*. This subsection states that chain once. Its first
link is unconditional; only the last requires bounded advantage and
score.

###### Proposition 10 (Behavioral Pinsker bound; restates and proves [proposition 2](#Thmproposition2 "Proposition 2 (Behavioral Pinsker bound on the conditioning gap). ‣ 5.2 What the residual KL guarantees ‣ 5 SDCC: Self-Distillation for Conditioning Consistency ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")).

For every diverging leaf $`p\in\mathcal{C}`$,

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\bigl\|p_{\theta}(\cdot\mid z_{p})-q_{\theta}(\cdot\mid x_{p})\bigr\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\;\leq\;\sqrt{\varepsilon_{p}(\theta)/2}.
``` |  | (27) |

###### Proof.

Pinsker’s inequality ([Tsybakov, 2009](#bib.bib42)) states that
$`\|\mu-\nu\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\leq\sqrt{D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\mu\|\nu)/2}`$ for
any two distributions on a common measurable space. Take
$`\mu=p_{\mathrm{sg}(\theta)}(\cdot\mid z_{p})`$ and
$`\nu=q_{\theta}(\cdot\mid x_{p})`$, whose divergence is exactly the
per-leaf SDCC residual $`\varepsilon_{p}(\theta)`$; at convergence the
stop-gradient branch equals $`p_{\theta}`$ and
equation [27](#A4.E27 "Equation 27 ‣ Proposition 10 (Behavioral Pinsker bound; restates and proves ). ‣ D.4 How the KL residual controls deployment and gradient bias ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
follows. No bounded-score, same-advantage or parameterization assumption
enters, so the bound is unconditional. Because the harness redelivers
$`z_{p}`$ at inference, the left-hand side is literally the deployment
gap: the behavioral distance between the context the update was computed
under and the one the deployed policy is served. ∎

###### Assumption 1 (Bounded advantage and last-layer score).

(A1) $`\|\hat{A}\|_{\infty}\leq A_{\max}`$; (A2) the same behavioral
advantage $`\hat{A}(y)`$ is used on both $`\mathbf{p_{t}}(y_{p})`$ and
$`\mathbf{p_{s}}(y_{p})`$; (A3) softmax parametrization with
$`\|h\|_{\infty}\leq H_{\max}`$, and the policy gradient is taken w.r.t.
the last-layer parameters, for which
$`\nabla_{\theta}\log\pi(y\mid c)=h_{y}(c)-\Exp_{y^{\prime}\sim\pi}[h_{y^{\prime}}(c)]`$
is uniformly bounded by $`2H_{\max}`$; (A4) advantages are averaged over
an outer batch.

###### Corollary 1 (Conditional gradient-bias bound).

Under
[Assumption 1](#Thmassumption1 "Assumption 1 (Bounded advantage and last-layer score). ‣ D.4 How the KL residual controls deployment and gradient bias ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”"),
the SDCC per-leaf policy-gradient deviation is
$`\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{\varepsilon_{p}})`$; in aggregate, with
$`C:=5A_{\max}H_{\max}`$,

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\Bigl\|\nabla_{\theta}\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{task}}(\theta;\mathbf{H}^{\mathrm{comp}})-\nabla_{\theta}\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{task}}^{\star}(\theta)\Bigr\|\;\leq\;C\sum_{p\in\mathcal{C}}\sqrt{\varepsilon_{p}/2}\;=\;\mathcal{O}\Bigl(\textstyle\sum_{p\in\mathcal{C}}\sqrt{\varepsilon_{p}}\Bigr),
``` |  | (28) |

where $`\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{task}}^{\star}`$ is the tree-consistent
task loss that 4D masks and LogitTree compute exactly. Writing
$`\varepsilon_{\mathrm{KL}}:=\max_{p}\varepsilon_{p}`$, this is the
per-leaf $`\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{KL}}})`$ form quoted
in
§[5.2](#S5.SS2 "5.2 What the residual KL guarantees ‣ 5 SDCC: Self-Distillation for Conditioning Consistency ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”").

###### Proof.

*Sketch: split the two policy gradients into a distribution-difference
term and a score-difference term; (A3) makes both Lipschitz in total
variation, which
[proposition 10](#Thmproposition10 "Proposition 10 (Behavioral Pinsker bound; restates and proves ). ‣ D.4 How the KL residual controls deployment and gradient bias ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
converts into $`\sqrt{\varepsilon_{p}}`$.*

Write $`\pi:=\pi_{\theta}(\cdot\mid\mathbf{p_{t}}(y_{p}))`$,
$`\widetilde{\pi}:=\pi_{\theta}(\cdot\mid\mathbf{p_{s}}(y_{p}))`$,
$`s_{\pi}(y):=\nabla_{\theta}\log\pi(y)`$,
$`g:=\sum_{y}\pi(y)\hat{A}(y)s_{\pi}(y)`$, and $`\tilde{g}`$ analogously
with the same $`\hat{A}`$ by (A2). Then

|  |  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle\|g-\tilde{g}\|`$ | $`\displaystyle\leq\Bigl\|\textstyle\sum_{y}\bigl(\pi(y)-\widetilde{\pi}(y)\bigr)\hat{A}(y)\,s_{\pi}(y)\Bigr\|+\Bigl\|\textstyle\sum_{y}\widetilde{\pi}(y)\hat{A}(y)\bigl(s_{\pi}(y)-s_{\widetilde{\pi}}(y)\bigr)\Bigr\|`$ |  |  |
|  |  | $`\displaystyle\leq 2A_{\max}H_{\max}\,\|\pi-\widetilde{\pi}\|_{1}\;+\;A_{\max}\,\Exp_{\widetilde{\pi}}\bigl\|s_{\pi}-s_{\widetilde{\pi}}\bigr\|.`$ |  | (29) |

Total variation is half the $`\ell_{1}`$ distance, so by (A1), (A3) and
[proposition 10](#Thmproposition10 "Proposition 10 (Behavioral Pinsker bound; restates and proves ). ‣ D.4 How the KL residual controls deployment and gradient bias ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
the first term is at most $`4A_{\max}H_{\max}\sqrt{\varepsilon_{p}/2}`$.
In the second, (A3) makes the two scores share $`h_{y}`$ at the query
token and differ only in the normalizer,
$`s_{\pi}(y)-s_{\widetilde{\pi}}(y)=\Exp_{\widetilde{\pi}}[h]-\Exp_{\pi}[h]`$,
bounded by
$`H_{\max}\|\pi-\widetilde{\pi}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\leq H_{\max}\sqrt{\varepsilon_{p}/2}`$
(scope:
[remark 1](#Thmremark1 "Remark 1 (Scope of the gradient corollary: last-layer restriction). ‣ D.4 How the KL residual controls deployment and gradient bias ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")).
Summing over per-leaf residuals and per-trajectory tokens as in (A4)
gives
equation [28](#A4.E28 "Equation 28 ‣ Corollary 1 (Conditional gradient-bias bound). ‣ D.4 How the KL residual controls deployment and gradient bias ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”").
∎

###### Remark 1 (Scope of the gradient corollary: last-layer restriction).

[proposition 2](#Thmproposition2 "Proposition 2 (Behavioral Pinsker bound on the conditioning gap). ‣ 5.2 What the residual KL guarantees ‣ 5 SDCC: Self-Distillation for Conditioning Consistency ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
is unconditional; only
[corollary 1](#Thmcorollary1 "Corollary 1 (Conditional gradient-bias bound). ‣ D.4 How the KL residual controls deployment and gradient bias ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
invokes
[Assumption 1](#Thmassumption1 "Assumption 1 (Bounded advantage and last-layer score). ‣ D.4 How the KL residual controls deployment and gradient bias ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”"),
where (A2) is the standard PPO/GRPO advantage-identifiability convention
and (A3) supplies the closed-form score. That identity needs $`\theta`$
to index the softmax head, so the two contexts share $`h_{y}`$ at the
query token and differ only in the normalizer $`\Exp_{\pi}[h]`$. For
full transformer parameters the score acquires an extra
$`\nabla_{\theta}h_{y}(c)`$ term that softmax structure alone does not
bound uniformly, and the corollary then needs a separate bound on
$`\|\nabla_{\theta}h_{y}(\mathbf{p_{t}})-\nabla_{\theta}h_{y}(\mathbf{p_{s}})\|`$,
e.g. via Lipschitz assumptions on the backbone. This restriction is
intrinsic to the ratio-difference decomposition, not an artifact of our
proof.

###### Corollary 2 (Rate to zero bias under training).

Under Assumptions (i)–(iv) of
§[D.6](#A4.SS6 "D.6 Convergence: contraction toward the zero-KL set ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”"),
Theorem [4](#Thmtheorem4 "Theorem 4 (Steady-state contraction toward zero-KL set). ‣ Steady-state contraction. ‣ D.6 Convergence: contraction toward the zero-KL set ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
yields
$`\min_{t\leq T}\Exp[\varepsilon_{p}(\theta_{t})]=\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{T})`$;
combined with
[corollary 1](#Thmcorollary1 "Corollary 1 (Conditional gradient-bias bound). ‣ D.4 How the KL residual controls deployment and gradient bias ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”"),
the deployment policy-gradient bias decays at the rate
$`\mathcal{O}(T^{-1/4})`$.

#### Cost, and where SDCC sits relative to the exact methods.

The bound above is what SDCC buys with its cost profile. SDCC requires
exactly one backward pass per trajectory against LogitTree’s $`K{+}1`$;
the teacher forwards share KV-cache trunks and are stop-gradient, so
they retain no activations. A 4D mask is cheaper still in pure FLOPs —
one forward, one backward — but requires attention-kernel surgery and
cannot be applied in black-box harnesses where eviction spans are never
exposed. The three methods therefore trade off along two independent
axes, correctness bias and infrastructure cost: the exact walks have
zero bias at heavy cost, while SDCC pays
$`\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{KL}}})`$ bias — decaying during
training by
[corollary 2](#Thmcorollary2 "Corollary 2 (Rate to zero bias under training). ‣ D.4 How the KL residual controls deployment and gradient bias ‣ Appendix D Full Variational Derivation of the SDCC Forward-KL Self-Distillation Loss ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
— for one backward pass and no kernel changes. The claim is not that
SDCC dominates the exact methods: where their cost is acceptable,
LogitTree and the 4D mask are the correctness ground truth; where it is
not, or in black-box regimes, SDCC is the only one of the three that
applies.

### D.5 LogitTree and SDCC optimize the same objective up to a $`\lambda`$-tunable slack

The exact walks of
[Figure 2](#S4.F2 "In 4 Exact Solutions: Two Ways to Walk the Context Tree ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
and SDCC of
[Section 5](#S5 "5 SDCC: Self-Distillation for Conditioning Consistency ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")
charge a diverging leaf $`p\in\mathcal{C}`$ in visibly different ways:
LogitTree places the policy loss on the pre-eviction branch
$`z_{p}=\mathbf{p_{t}}(y_{p})`$, so its per-leaf loss is an expectation
under the teacher distribution $`p_{\theta}(\cdot\mid z_{p})`$; SDCC
keeps the policy loss on the compressed branch
$`x_{p}=\mathbf{p_{s}}(y_{p})`$, so its per-leaf loss is an expectation
under the student distribution $`q_{\theta}(\cdot\mid x_{p})`$,
augmented with a stop-gradient forward KL that penalizes the two
distributions for disagreeing
(§[5.1](#S5.SS1 "5.1 Aligning the live and compressed trajectories ‣ 5 SDCC: Self-Distillation for Conditioning Consistency ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”")).
The two constructions therefore differ in *which* branch of
$`\mathcal{T}`$ enters the policy loss — LogitTree scores every branch
(Prop. [3](#Thmproposition3 "Proposition 3 (SFT and RL equivalence on the tree). ‣ C.1 Per-branch equivalence on the tree ( and ) ‣ Appendix C Proofs ‣ MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw “Your Memory-Compressing Harness Makes Training and Inference Inconsistent”"));
SDCC scores only the deployed branch and charges the others through the
KL. Because the KL residual controls the behavioral gap between the two
branches
````
